note: Invented pilot histories for the Squadron Room, written in the plain voice of the example Patrick gave on 21 September 2026. Every route is a real way into a fighter cockpit by the summer of 1940; the men are invented. A story is the route's four paragraphs (the side's closing is empty). The last paragraph is not personal: it is the short entry his new commanding officer finds in the file, where he is posted and how he was assessed. Computed tokens: {first} {last} {name} {born} {year} {age} {place} {town} {joined} {type} {unit} {base}, and on the British side {posted} {hours} {ontype} {otu}. Anything else is looked up in the side's lists, one item picked from a number made from the pilot's name and reused if the token appears again. Rules for the lists: plain sentences, subject first, no semicolons, no clever endings; only the home lists mention a father; the mother is always alive; nothing that has to happen by the sea or on a farm. Check any change with dev/render_backgrounds.py.

text: {name} was born in {town} on {born} and grew up {home}. He attended {school}, {boyhood}. At sixteen, he left school to become {job}.

He had wanted to fly since {spark}, but lessons were well beyond his wages. Joining the RAF Volunteer Reserve in {joined} gave him the opportunity. He trained at weekends at {erfts}, learning on Tiger Moths before progressing to the Hawker Hart. {moment}

Called up on 1 September 1939, he spent several weeks waiting for a training place. He completed his initial instruction at {itwplace}, then moved to {sfts}, where he flew {trainer} and qualified as a sergeant pilot. A short conversion course at {otu} followed. He finished it with roughly {hours} flying hours, but only {ontype} on {type}s and little gunnery practice.

{name} was born in {town} on {born} and grew up {home}. He attended {school}, {boyhood}. At fifteen he passed the entrance examination for an RAF aircraft apprenticeship.

He spent three years at No. 1 School of Technical Training at Halton and passed out as {trade}. He then served on a squadron, looking after the aircraft he hoped one day to fly. A few former apprentices were chosen for pilot training each year, and in {joined} he was one of them.

He learned to fly at {erfts} and then went on to {sfts}, where he flew {trainer} and qualified as a sergeant pilot. {moment} A short conversion course at {otu} followed. He came to fighters knowing far more about engines and airframes than most of his fellow pilots.

{name} was born in {town} on {born} and grew up {homeoff}. He was educated at {pubschool}, where he {boyhoodoff}. He left school at eighteen and worked for a year as {offjob}.

He had wanted to fly since {spark}. In {joined} he answered an Air Ministry advertisement for short service commissions, which offered four years of flying followed by six on the reserve. He learned to fly as a civilian at {civschool}, then spent a fortnight at the RAF Depot at Uxbridge on drill and uniform fittings before being commissioned as an acting pilot officer.
He finished his training at {sfts}, where he flew {trainer} and was awarded his wings. {moment} He was then posted to fighters and learned to fly the {type} with his squadron.

He passed out with a permanent commission and was posted to a fighter squadron. He converted to the {type} when the squadron was re-equipped shortly before the war, and he now has more experience than most of the pilots around him.

text: {name} was born in {town} on {born} and grew up {home}. He attended {school}, {boyhood}. After leaving school he began {job}.

Germany was not allowed an air force under the Treaty of Versailles, and gliding was how most young Germans of his age first learned to fly. He learned to glide {glide}, gaining his A, B and C gliding certificates. After six months in the Reich Labour Service he was called up in {joined} and accepted by the Luftwaffe for pilot training.

After basic training he went to {ab}, where he gained his A and B licences on the Focke-Wulf Stieglitz, the Bücker Jungmann and the Arado 66. {moment} He was selected for fighters and sent to {jfs}, where he flew the Arado 68 and early versions of the Bf 109. He reached the front through the Ergänzungsjagdgruppe at Merseburg.
